fatal_errors: The proposed coating and unspecified adhesion promoter do not reconstruct the target intervention, which varied Mo content within Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composites.
The evidence for the dichalcogenide nanoflakes concerns ambient-temperature steel-on-steel testing and does not support stability, adhesion, or lubrication on CoCrFeNi at 800 °C.

The baseline is mischaracterized as bare CoCrFeNi with friction and wear rising monotonically with temperature; the target baseline is a Mo0.2 self-lubricating composite with friction and wear peaking at intermediate temperatures and decreasing strongly by 800 °C.
The predicted coefficient of friction below 0.1 and order-of-magnitude wear reduction across the entire range are unsupported extrapolations.
The proposed carbonaceous tribofilm mechanism is speculative and unsupported by either cited source.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general wide-temperature friction-and-wear problem and offers a novel, testable coating concept, but it has little agreement with the hidden study. The target relies on Mo-driven lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening together with low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication and high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation. The generated mechanism only overlaps at the broad level of forming a protective high-temperature glaze. Its test conditions omit essential controls such as counterface, sliding speed, distance, and discrete temperature holds, while the proposed temperature ramp could confound thermal history with temperature response. The three-arm comparison and microscopy/XRD measurements provide moderate discriminability, although the falsification rule combines an arbitrary COF threshold with statistical improvement and delamination. Most importantly, the cited evidence does not validate the full-temperature claim: E2 supports low friction for sprayed nanoflakes on steel in ambient conditions, while E1 supports high-temperature oxide glaze formation in a different bulk alloy architecture. Neither establishes that the proposed sulfide coating or adhesion promoter survives and performs from room temperature through 800 °C on CoCrFeNi.
